business_problem: KPMG UK needed to redesign internal IT support before renewing major managed-service contracts because routine incidents were interrupting consultants, support requests moved through multiple teams, and the firm lacked proof that a more automated model would pay off.
solution_summary: KPMG UK treated its contract-renewal window as a chance to build an AI-first service model instead of just extending the old one. A ServiceNow IT Service Management value assessment identified where automation could reshape incident economics, after which an internal team with no previous AI experience completed an immersive sprint and launched 22 production AI use cases in 85 working days. Employees now start in Microsoft Teams, where ServiceNow AI Agents understand who they are, where they are based, and device health before resolving routine issues or routing work into the broader ITSM flow. ServiceNow Impact provided the prioritization framework, governance cadence, and architecture support that let the team scale quickly without chaos. With the old and new experiences running in parallel during rollout, KPMG gained a repeatable proof of value that not only changed vendor negotiations but also became a client-facing blueprint for enterprise AI adoption.
